sources.entry: TileServer GL - Vector and raster maps with GL styles. Server side rendering by Mapbox GL Native. Map tile server for Mapbox GL JS, Android, iOS, Leaflet, OpenLayers, GIS via WMTS, etc. (Source Code) BSD-2-Clause Nodejs/Docker

summary.one_liner: TileServer GL is a map tile server that serves vector and raster maps built from GL styles, with server-side raster rendering via MapLibre GL Native.
summary.what_it_does: Serves vector tiles (for example from MBTiles files) and renders them to raster images on the server using MapLibre GL Native. It is meant to feed web and mobile map clients such as MapLibre GL JS, Android, iOS, Leaflet and OpenLayers, and GIS software via WMTS. Setup can use a single mbtiles file or a config.json with style and data files. The README also describes a pure-JavaScript tileserver-gl-light variant with no native dependencies, which skips server-side rasterization. It is installable via npm or run as a Docker image, and includes a Host header poisoning mitigation using a --public_url flag or the TILESERVER_GL_ALLOWED_HOSTS environment variable.
use_cases: serve vector map tiles to a web map
host offline mbtiles maps on a local server
provide WMTS map tiles to GIS software
render raster map images from GL styles on the server
feed tiles to Leaflet or OpenLayers apps
self-host map tiles for mobile apps
notable: Server-side raster rendering of GL styles through MapLibre GL Native
Two flavors: tileserver-gl with native rendering and tileserver-gl-light as pure JavaScript
Serves WMTS, TileJSON and style JSON endpoints for map clients
Documented Host header poisoning mitigation with --public_url and an allowed-hosts list
caveats: Running without Docker requires native dependencies to be installed first
Server-side rasterization is not available in the tileserver-gl-light variant
Without --public_url, the allowed-hosts default is '*', so all hosts are accepted unless configured
